core.title: Make the runtime load and resolve from the declared route space, not transcribe it
core.given: A consumer declares a route space in its plan artifacts
core.when: The consumer's runtime surface is written, changed or assessed — including when no runtime exists yet
core.then: The consumer MUST have a runtime that reads the declaration it is given and resolves from what it read: a component constructed with a declaration loads that declaration and resolves from the loaded data, and element order comes from the declared sequence definition when one is declared.
prefer: Load the declaration and resolve from the loaded data; loading may live in a sibling module within the runtime surface.
Resolve through a by-key accessor over the loaded declaration rather than an inline filter.
avoid: Transcription: storing the declaration reference and returning hardcoded resolution results, or a literal key-to-elements map, that match the declaration today.
Treating passing text-level correspondence checks as proof that the plan is executed.
unless: The consumer declares no route space.
A runtime that loads the declaration is never checked for declaration literals.
core.why: A transcribing runtime matches the plan when written, then diverges silently as the plan is edited while every literal-correspondence check still passes; an absent runtime at least fails loudly. Reading the declaration makes the plan the runtime's source of truth.
evidence: Some module within the runtime surface loads the declaration file (a read/parse construct the profile recognizes) and the runtime resolves from that data.

Divergence probe: introducing a declared route the runtime cannot resolve, an element sequence that contradicts the runtime, or deleting the plan artifacts entirely must be detected or break execution, rather than letting the application keep running.
verification: Severity 2; disposition strict — the convention run fails on every finding, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

The loading check is evaluated over the whole runtime surface rather than per module, because a correct implementation may delegate loading to a sibling module within that surface; a declared route space with no runtime surface at all violates the obligation to have a reading runtime.

Transcription, the failure the check flags: resolution results and element order are literals that happen to match the declaration today; the runtime agrees with the plan when written and cannot disagree detectably afterwards, because nothing compares them at runtime.

The unreachable-route check is only ever evaluated against a transcribing (non-loading) runtime; a runtime that loads the declaration is never checked for declaration literals — it serves every declared route by construction, and flagging the absent literal would punish the correct implementation for being correct.
Literal correspondence does not prove declaration execution: a transcribing runtime can satisfy every check that compares literals in code with literals in the plan while the code never reads it.
The check must be wired into the gated repository-wide scan for enforcement to run; a check that exists but is not called by the gate enforces nothing.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds involved: the route-space declaration whose presence alone triggers the obligation, and the element-sequence definitions whose order the runtime must read when they are declared.
Where the modules of the plan-executing runtime live; together they form the runtime surface that is checked as a whole for loading the declaration (in Bun, a consumer-configured runtime selector).
How the stack recognizes that a module reads and parses a plan-declaration file, so the loading check has concrete constructs to look for.

proposedKeys.meaning: Where the modules forming the plan-executing runtime live (a path segment or glob); they are checked as one runtime surface, not per module.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The closed role list has no role for the component that executes the declared plan — it is neither the application layer nor delivery machinery — and no layout or idiom key holds a selector for it. Adopting the key means adding 'runtime' to the roles params.

proposedKeys.meaning: The constructs by which a module in this stack reads and parses a plan-declaration file, so a check can recognize that the runtime loads the declaration.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No existing idiom covers reading/parsing plan artifacts: validation_shape is request validation, machinery is delivery machinery, markup_kinds is declarative markup.

neutralityNotes: The obligation is fully neutral: a consumer that declares a route space must have a runtime that reads the declaration and resolves from the loaded data, with element order taken from declared sequence definitions when they exist — never transcribed — and the rule applies from the moment the route space is declared, including when no runtime surface exists yet (the absent runtime is itself the violation, not an excuse). What could not be made neutral: (1) the plan domain — guarded interlocking routes, train definitions, wagon order, dispatch — is the worked example's content; it lives in bun.json plus the plan-artifact kinds profile key, and the core speaks of a route space and element sequences. (2) The concrete runtime component names (InterlockingRunner, TrainRunner) and the constructs that count as loading a declaration are per-stack data; no vocabulary key exists for either, so roles.runtime.path and idiom.declaration_load are proposed. (3) Bun's path_glob activation fact has no slot in the neutral fact vocabulary and is re-expressed as a role fact over the runtime surface. (4) Two verifier facts are Bun-only: the bilateral-binding provenance scanner's inability to trace inline filters (reported as undecidable rather than passed) — another stack's checker could trace them — and this rule's exclusive position as the Bun package's only loading check among otherwise literal-correspondence rules. The core keeps only the neutral by-key accessor preference and the general warning that literal correspondence does not prove declaration execution.
